Present in codes and complex laws. Format: TÍTULO I, TÍTULO PRELIMINAR.
Most common higher division in ordinary laws. Format: CAPÍTULO I.
Grouping above artículos in codes only. Always a higher division, never the basic unit. Format: Sección 1ª.
Basic citable unit. Format: Art. 1°.– or Artículo 1°.– Numbered continuously throughout law.

Second-level subdivision within inciso. Format: 1., 2., 3. Used in technical and commercial legislation.

structuring.prompt_additions: Argentina uses ARTICLE (not SECTION) as the basic unit. Use ARTICLE for every artículo. Higher divisions: BOOK (libro, codes only), TITLE (título), CHAPTER (capítulo), SUBDIVISION (sección as grouping in codes). First-level subdivisions within articles are PARAGRAPH for incisos (a), b), c)). Second-level subdivisions are POINT for sub-incisos. No marginal notes — article headings are inline after the article number and dash. Insertion numbering uses bis/ter/quater (Artículo 5° bis). Law numbers are continuous integers without year component (Ley 27742). Strip degree symbols from article numbers in eIds (Artículo 1° → art_1).

supranational_memberships.note: MERCOSUR is explicitly non-supranational. All instruments require domestic incorporation. Incorporated instruments are modelled as ordinary leyes.
UN SC Chapter VII resolutions are binding obligations but require domestic implementation. Human rights treaties listed in Art. 75(22) CN have constitutional rank above ordinary laws.

display.heading_note: Article headings appear inline after the article number and dash: 'Artículo 1°.– Objeto.' Not marginal notes.
